accessibility-audit.what: Review an interface for accessibility barriers.
accessibility-audit.when: An accessibility audit or a check of requested fixes.
accessibility-audit.inputs: The interface, relevant user journeys, and the target standard.
accessibility-audit.outputs: Findings with reproduction steps, affected criteria, proposed repairs, and coverage gaps.
accessibility-audit.example: Audit this checkout flow against WCAG 2.2 AA and give me reproducible findings.

analytics-strategy.what: Define what to measure and how to collect it.
analytics-strategy.when: A measurement plan, event taxonomy, or decision-focused dashboard.
analytics-strategy.inputs: Business decisions, user journeys, existing metrics, and data constraints.
analytics-strategy.outputs: Metric definitions, event specifications, and a measurement or dashboard plan.
analytics-strategy.example: Define the events and metrics we need to understand where onboarding stalls.

architecture-doc.what: Explain a system’s architecture in a sourced reference document.
architecture-doc.when: A formal architecture or technical design reference.
architecture-doc.inputs: Source material, design decisions, system constraints, and the selected brand.
architecture-doc.outputs: Architecture intent, component and interface views, data design, and trade-offs.
architecture-doc.example: Write an architecture reference from this design record, including interfaces and trade-offs.

beastmode-capture.what: Save a decision or correction in Megan’s knowledge system.
beastmode-capture.when: Megan asks to retain a supported decision, discovery, or correction.
beastmode-capture.inputs: The decision, supporting evidence, intended destination, and current record.
beastmode-capture.outputs: A verified saved record or revision proposal with its actual acceptance state.
beastmode-capture.example: Save this decision in the current BeastMode project record with its supporting source.
beastmode-capture.reuseNote: This adapter saves decisions to Megan’s permitted BeastMode records under her knowledge contract.

beastmode-context.what: Resume Megan’s work from the current subject sources.
beastmode-context.when: A request to get oriented or continue a BeastMode project.
beastmode-context.inputs: The requested result and access to the relevant local sources or permitted Hub.
beastmode-context.outputs: The relevant context, source conflicts, and the next supported action.
beastmode-context.example: Resume this BeastMode project from its current sources and identify the next action.
beastmode-context.reuseNote: This workflow follows Megan’s BeastMode router to her current private subject authorities.

beastmode-health.what: Check Megan’s context and knowledge infrastructure.
beastmode-health.when: A Hub health check or investigation of stale context.
beastmode-health.inputs: The permitted Hub connection and the named environment or symptom.
beastmode-health.outputs: Scoped health findings, evidence, and any remaining checks.
beastmode-health.example: Check the local Hub for stale context and report the evidence behind each finding.
beastmode-health.reuseNote: The health checks depend on Megan’s configured Hub connection and operating environment.

beastmode-reconcile.what: Compare Megan’s source folders and preserve unique evidence.
beastmode-reconcile.when: A named intake, reconciliation, or authorized cleanup task.
beastmode-reconcile.inputs: The folders, current authorities, and existing reconciliation records.
beastmode-reconcile.outputs: A comparison and, when authorized, verified reversible dispositions.
beastmode-reconcile.example: Compare these two project folders and identify unique material before proposing any moves.
beastmode-reconcile.reuseNote: The reconciliation rules use Megan’s two source drives, existing disposition records, and cleanup permissions.

brain-work-item.what: Connect a Codex work item to Megan’s Brain task record.
brain-work-item.when: Starting, continuing, or completing a Brain-linked task.
brain-work-item.inputs: The task ID, current Brain note, and access to the task bridge.
brain-work-item.outputs: The task’s supported state, work receipt, and linked chat where applicable.
brain-work-item.example: Continue this Brain task and record the result when its acceptance checks pass.
brain-work-item.reuseNote: The workflow calls MeganOS task helpers and reads Megan’s Brain task records.

brand-renderer.what: Render an artifact using the selected visual identity.
brand-renderer.when: A document, deck, workbook, PDF, or page needs branded rendering.
brand-renderer.inputs: The artifact, confirmed brand profile or neutral defaults, and rendering runtime.
brand-renderer.outputs: Rendered files, brand checks, and findings from visual inspection.
brand-renderer.example: Render this report using the confirmed project brand and inspect the exported pages.

business-case.what: Build the case for an investment decision.
business-case.when: An approver needs to decide whether to fund an initiative.
business-case.inputs: The problem, alternatives, supported benefits, costs, risks, and funding decision.
business-case.outputs: An investment case with shown calculations, trade-offs, and a bounded ask.
business-case.example: Build an investment case from these costs, benefits, and alternatives for the funding owner.

call-prep.what: Prepare a pursuit or an upcoming sales conversation.
call-prep.when: A pursuit brief, call objective, agenda, or stakeholder plan is needed.
call-prep.inputs: Account evidence, attendees, pursuit context, and the upcoming decision.
call-prep.outputs: A pursuit or call brief with ranked questions and recommended next steps.
call-prep.example: Prepare a call brief for this account with an objective, agenda, and ranked questions.

career-application.what: Prepare Megan’s application and interview work for a selected role.
career-application.when: Assessing a posting, tailoring materials, or preparing an interview.
career-application.inputs: The current posting, Megan’s career sources, and the role work record.
career-application.outputs: Role assessment, tailored materials, interview preparation, or authorized form work.
career-application.example: Assess this posting against my current career direction and prepare the selected application materials.
career-application.reuseNote: The workflow depends on Megan’s private career records, target roles, role tracker, and writing profile.

career-materials-and-outreach.what: Draft supporting application materials in Megan’s voice.
career-materials-and-outreach.when: A cover letter, form answer, outreach draft, or LinkedIn section is needed.
career-materials-and-outreach.inputs: The role record, current career evidence, and the requested audience.
career-materials-and-outreach.outputs: Complete drafts tied to the role and Megan’s supported experience.
career-materials-and-outreach.example: Draft a cover letter for this role from my current role work record.
career-materials-and-outreach.reuseNote: Megan is the intended author. The workflow uses her role record, career evidence, and voice.

career-progression-and-offers.what: Compare roles and offers against Megan’s career direction.
career-progression-and-offers.when: A role screen, tracker review, negotiation, or offer comparison.
career-progression-and-offers.inputs: Role or offer terms, Megan’s criteria, and the current career record.
career-progression-and-offers.outputs: A comparison, open questions, and negotiation drafts for Megan’s decision.
career-progression-and-offers.example: Compare these offers against my recorded career gates and list the unresolved terms.
career-progression-and-offers.reuseNote: The criteria and decisions follow Megan’s VP-to-ELT direction, personal career gates, and offer tracker.

case-study-builder.what: Turn Megan’s work into a portfolio case study.
case-study-builder.when: A project or engagement needs a case study for her portfolio.
case-study-builder.inputs: Project evidence, her template, and current claims and rights decisions.
case-study-builder.outputs: A working copy and a clean publish copy with unresolved gaps kept in the working record.
case-study-builder.example: Turn this project into a working case study and publish copy using my claims ledger.
case-study-builder.reuseNote: The workflow writes Megan’s portfolio and depends on her project evidence, claims ledger, and publication rights.

client-brand.what: Apply the confirmed project or client identity.
client-brand.when: An artifact needs a brand profile or existing profile applied.
client-brand.inputs: The project’s confirmed colors, typography, assets, and usage rights.
client-brand.outputs: A selected or updated profile and an artifact checked against it.
client-brand.example: Apply this confirmed brand profile to the document and check the rendered result.

code-simplify.what: Improve code clarity while preserving its behavior.
code-simplify.when: An authorized change needs a simplification or reuse review.
code-simplify.inputs: The current diff, repository conventions, and relevant behavior checks.
code-simplify.outputs: Focused refinements and evidence that the required behavior remains intact.
code-simplify.example: Review this diff for duplication and unnecessary complexity while preserving its behavior.

cross-platform-skill-release.what: Package a skill for Codex and Claude destinations.
cross-platform-skill-release.when: A shared skill needs packaging, replacement, or destination inspection.
cross-platform-skill-release.inputs: The source package, target hosts, and supported installation or upload path.
cross-platform-skill-release.outputs: A portable release package and separately verified destination states.
cross-platform-skill-release.example: Package this reviewed skill for the specified Codex and Claude destinations.

cutover-closeout.what: Prepare cutover, hypercare, and delivery closeout.
cutover-closeout.when: An accepted release is approaching go-live or closeout.
cutover-closeout.inputs: Executed scope, release evidence, owners, and the go or no-go decision.
cutover-closeout.outputs: A cutover runbook, acceptance record, hypercare plan, and closeout materials.
cutover-closeout.example: Prepare the cutover runbook and hypercare plan from this accepted release.

ddoc.what: Build a deck for a scope or proposal decision.
ddoc.when: A buyer needs to compare options or confirm one proposal direction.
ddoc.inputs: Scoped options, supporting evidence, commercial inputs, and the decision mode.
ddoc.outputs: A reviewed decision narrative and editable presentation.
ddoc.example: Build a decision deck comparing these two scoped options for the buyer.

deal-desk.what: Review a deal’s commercial figures and approval conditions.
deal-desk.when: An internal commercial review or quote tie-out is needed.
deal-desk.inputs: One quote revision, provider economics, and the applicable approval policy.
deal-desk.outputs: A commercial review packet with reconciled figures and approval gaps.
deal-desk.example: Reconcile this proposal against the quote and prepare the internal commercial review.

deck-builder.what: Build a presentation around the audience’s decision.
deck-builder.when: A pitch, proposal, reading deck, or technical briefing is needed.
deck-builder.inputs: The audience, decision, source evidence, and output requirements.
deck-builder.outputs: An editable deck with reviewed copy, explanatory visuals, and rendered checks.
deck-builder.example: Create a briefing deck that helps this audience decide between the supported options.

delivery-kickoff.when: The sales-to-delivery handoff is accepted and kickoff is next.
delivery-kickoff.inputs: The signed SOW, accepted handoff, team, and governance requirements.
delivery-kickoff.outputs: A charter, governance pack, kickoff materials, and initial delivery plan.
delivery-kickoff.example: Prepare kickoff materials from the signed SOW and accepted handoff.

delivery-status.what: Report delivery progress against the agreed scope.
delivery-status.when: A status report, risk update, decision log, or scope check is needed.
delivery-status.inputs: The executed baseline, reporting period, progress evidence, and current logs.
delivery-status.outputs: A status report, maintained logs, and supported scope-change candidates.
delivery-status.example: Write this period’s delivery status from the executed scope and current progress records.

delivery-suite.what: Route delivery work to the appropriate stage and owner.
delivery-suite.when: A signed engagement needs coordination across delivery stages.
delivery-suite.inputs: Executed scope, current delivery state, and the requested decision.
delivery-suite.outputs: An updated stage record and the next owning workflow or gate.
delivery-suite.example: Review this engagement’s delivery state and route the next work to its owner.

discovery-brief.what: Maintain the findings and open questions for a pursuit.
discovery-brief.when: Preparing discovery or incorporating a completed call.
discovery-brief.inputs: The pursuit record, source notes, and scope or pricing questions.
discovery-brief.outputs: A sourced discovery ledger and ranked questions that unblock the pursuit.
discovery-brief.example: Update the pursuit ledger from this call and rank the unanswered scope questions.

discovery-synthesis.what: Turn interviews and meeting notes into research findings.
discovery-synthesis.inputs: Transcripts, notes, speaker context, and the research purpose.
discovery-synthesis.outputs: Supported findings, jobs to be done, pain points, quotations, and next steps.
discovery-synthesis.example: Synthesize these interviews into findings, jobs to be done, and supported next steps.

dx-devops-promote.what: Prepare and perform an authorized DevOps Center promotion.
dx-devops-promote.when: Work items or a pipeline stage need promotion.
dx-devops-promote.inputs: The configured integration, target stage, work items, and authorization.
dx-devops-promote.outputs: Capability and dependency checks, promotion results, and unresolved conflicts.
dx-devops-promote.example: Check whether these work items are ready for promotion to the specified stage.

dx-devops-work-item-manage.what: Manage DevOps Center work items and review requests.
dx-devops-work-item-manage.when: Creating, updating, committing, or reviewing a work item.
dx-devops-work-item-manage.inputs: The configured integration, selected work item, and requested operation.
dx-devops-work-item-manage.outputs: The verified work-item change, commit, or review request.
dx-devops-work-item-manage.example: Inspect this DevOps Center work item and prepare the requested field update.

evidence-core.what: Track source records and the claims an artifact can support.
evidence-core.when: A material client artifact needs evidence review.
evidence-core.inputs: The project sources, revisions, authority rules, and proposed claims.
evidence-core.outputs: A source register, atomic claims, conflicts, and an evidence sufficiency decision.
evidence-core.example: Build a claim ledger for this report using these versioned sources.

execution-truth.what: Verify what changed and where the result exists.
execution-truth.when: Work changes files, repositories, deployments, installations, or cloud records.
execution-truth.inputs: The intended result, affected destination, and available verification access.
execution-truth.outputs: A precise completion state with evidence and the remaining action.
execution-truth.example: Verify which parts of this release are local, merged, published, and installed.

fortunes-weave.what: Answer questions and maintain Megan’s Fortune’s Weave planner.
fortunes-weave.when: A question concerns her current route, roster, or planner.
fortunes-weave.inputs: Her current project router, route sources, roster, and live planner state.
fortunes-weave.outputs: A sourced answer or an authorized, verified planner update.
fortunes-weave.example: Check my current route and roster before recommending the next planner update.
fortunes-weave.reuseNote: The workflow uses Megan’s route, roster, project router, and planner state.

github-repository-work.when: A repository needs inspection, a commit, a PR, or release work.
github-repository-work.inputs: The intended mshellman-llc repository and authorized change.
github-repository-work.outputs: Verified repository changes and separate PR, merge, or deployment state.
github-repository-work.example: Review this mshellman-llc repository change and prepare a pull request.
github-repository-work.reuseNote: The entrypoint selects the mshellman-llc account. Another owner needs an explicit repository and identity configuration.

independent-product.what: Develop Megan’s independent work from supplied historical projects.
independent-product.when: An employer-era artifact is being translated into an independent product or offer.
independent-product.inputs: Authorized historical sources, a project brief, and claims and rights decisions.
independent-product.outputs: A usable independent artifact or backlog with source and publication questions resolved where possible.
independent-product.example: Translate these authorized historical materials into an independent offering brief.
independent-product.reuseNote: The entrypoint carries Megan’s historical reuse authorization and private project routes. Those permissions do not transfer to another user.

information-architecture.what: Organize navigation, content labels, and site structure.
information-architecture.when: A website or product needs better findability.
information-architecture.inputs: The audience, content inventory, tasks, and current navigation.
information-architecture.outputs: A sitemap, taxonomy, navigation proposal, or structural review.
information-architecture.example: Reorganize this site’s navigation around the tasks visitors need to complete.

interactive-proposal.what: Build a page for exploring scope options.
interactive-proposal.when: A priced proposal or an unpriced scope explorer is needed.
interactive-proposal.inputs: Versioned scope, options, assumptions, and confirmed prices when applicable.
interactive-proposal.outputs: An interactive HTML page with selectable options and reconciled figures.
interactive-proposal.example: Create an interactive comparison of these scope options using the confirmed quote figures.

journey-mapping.what: Map a customer or role’s experience and the service underneath.
journey-mapping.when: A journey map, service blueprint, or opportunity map is needed.
journey-mapping.inputs: Touchpoints, research, goals, friction, roles, and system evidence.
journey-mapping.outputs: A journey or blueprint with sourced findings and labeled hypotheses.
journey-mapping.example: Map this customer journey from research through the service and systems underneath.

jtbd-framing.what: Frame the job a person is trying to accomplish.
jtbd-framing.when: Job statements, hire criteria, or switching triggers need analysis.
jtbd-framing.inputs: Research about struggling moments, switching triggers, and desired outcomes.
jtbd-framing.outputs: Job statements, hire and fire criteria, and a review of unsupported framing.
jtbd-framing.example: Extract the struggling moments and hire criteria from these interviews before drafting job statements.

knowledge-hub.what: Retrieve and maintain a project’s durable knowledge.
knowledge-hub.when: Work needs current client, pursuit, engagement, or evidence records.
knowledge-hub.inputs: The confirmed project identity, permitted storage, and relevant sources.
knowledge-hub.outputs: Retrieved context or verified workspace and record updates.
knowledge-hub.example: Find the current discovery and decision records for this opportunity in the permitted store.

megan-writing-style.what: Write prose in Megan’s personal voice.
megan-writing-style.when: Megan is the intended author of the finished text.
megan-writing-style.inputs: The draft or brief, its sources, and her current voice guidance.
megan-writing-style.outputs: Complete prose reviewed against her personal writing preferences.
megan-writing-style.example: Rewrite this About draft in my voice while preserving its supported claims.
megan-writing-style.reuseNote: This is Megan’s personal voice profile. Another author should build and confirm a separate profile.

org-preflight.what: Verify the Salesforce organization before a write.
org-preflight.when: A Salesforce record change, upload, or deployment is about to occur.
org-preflight.inputs: The intended org ID, sandbox status, connection, and requested action.
org-preflight.outputs: A current identity check and a proceed or stop decision.
org-preflight.example: Verify the intended Salesforce org ID and sandbox status before this record update.

personal-writing-style-runtime.what: Apply one person’s confirmed writing profile.
personal-writing-style-runtime.when: The intended author has an approved private style profile.
personal-writing-style-runtime.inputs: That author’s profile, its scope, and a configured installation adapter.
personal-writing-style-runtime.outputs: Writing reviewed against the selected author’s profile.
personal-writing-style-runtime.example: Apply the confirmed author profile to this draft within its stated scope.

playbook-builder.what: Define and maintain a productized service offering.
playbook-builder.when: An offering needs definition, comparison, or catalog maintenance.
playbook-builder.inputs: The buyer, problem, proposed service, scope, and current catalog.
playbook-builder.outputs: A structured offering with value, deliverables, boundaries, and catalog decisions.
playbook-builder.example: Define the buyer, value, deliverables, and boundaries for this service offering.

playbook-fit-router.what: Match a prospect’s needs to an offering.
playbook-fit-router.when: Discovery needs to become an offering-fit decision.
playbook-fit-router.inputs: The current offering catalog and supported prospect findings.
playbook-fit-router.outputs: Ranked fit, evidence behind the score, disqualifiers, and open questions.
playbook-fit-router.example: Compare this prospect’s discovery findings with our current offering catalog.

playbook-onepager.what: Render an offering into sales handouts.
playbook-onepager.when: A defined offering needs internal enablement or an external handout.
playbook-onepager.inputs: Structured offering content and the selected brand profile.
playbook-onepager.outputs: A two-page internal brief and one-page external PDF, checked after rendering.
playbook-onepager.example: Render this defined offering as an internal brief and an external handout.

playbook-suite.what: Plan and track the artifacts for an offering.
playbook-suite.when: An offering needs a complete artifact package or readiness review.
playbook-suite.inputs: The offering definition, manifest, existing artifacts, and commercial policy.
playbook-suite.outputs: An artifact plan, owning workflows, and remaining readiness checks.
playbook-suite.example: Review this offering’s artifact manifest and identify what remains before release.

pm-spec-writing.when: A feature needs a PRD, development brief, or acceptance criteria.
pm-spec-writing.inputs: The problem, users, evidence, constraints, and requested scope.
pm-spec-writing.outputs: A specification with behavior, requirements, and testable acceptance criteria.
pm-spec-writing.example: Write a feature specification with user behavior, requirements, and acceptance criteria.

process.what: Document a process or identify improvements.
process.when: An SOP, ownership map, or process optimization is needed.
process.inputs: The current steps, roles, exceptions, constraints, and available measures.
process.outputs: An SOP or improvement analysis covering time, cost, quality, and ownership.
process.example: Document this approval process as an SOP with owners, exceptions, and measures.

product-development-pathway.what: Develop a product from its current evidence and release state.
product-development-pathway.when: Starting or resuming a product at a requested stage.
product-development-pathway.inputs: The product brief, current sources, decisions, and readiness evidence.
product-development-pathway.outputs: An updated product record and the next supported development action.
product-development-pathway.example: Resume this product at its current stage using the recorded readiness evidence.

prose-pass.what: Run writing diagnostics and preserve figures during revision.
prose-pass.when: Writing-integrity needs a scanner or a review record.
prose-pass.inputs: The saved text, source figures, and required review configuration.
prose-pass.outputs: Diagnostic findings, figure comparisons, or review records.
prose-pass.example: Check this saved draft for recurring writing patterns and changed figures.

quality-gate.what: Review a finished artifact against the request and sources.
quality-gate.when: A material deliverable is approaching release.
quality-gate.inputs: The artifact, controlling sources, output requirements, and actual checks.
quality-gate.outputs: A release decision with supported findings and required repairs.
quality-gate.example: Review this deliverable against its sources, requested outcome, and rendered form.

requirements-capture.what: Turn source material into a structured requirements backlog.
requirements-capture.when: Requirements, user stories, or a SOW-to-backlog workbook is needed.
requirements-capture.inputs: The brief, SOW, transcripts, or product sources and project context.
requirements-capture.outputs: A workbook of epics, capabilities, needs, stories, and acceptance criteria.
requirements-capture.example: Turn this SOW into a requirements workbook with stories and testable acceptance criteria.

resume-numbers-and-keywords.what: Apply Megan’s resume methods for figures and ATS wording.
resume-numbers-and-keywords.when: Her tailored resume needs quantified bullets or keyword placement.
resume-numbers-and-keywords.inputs: Current career evidence, the posting, and the draft resume.
resume-numbers-and-keywords.outputs: Revised bullets and layout that preserve her stated scope and evidence.
resume-numbers-and-keywords.example: Review my resume bullets against this posting and the current source figures.
resume-numbers-and-keywords.reuseNote: The method includes Megan’s actual deal figures, career-source names, and dated resume decisions. Other authors need their own evidence and preferences.

rom.what: Estimate a rough effort or cost range.
rom.when: A pursuit needs an early estimate and its basis.
rom.inputs: Supplied scope, comparables, assumptions, and rates when available.
rom.outputs: A sourced estimate range with calculations and reopening conditions.
rom.example: Estimate a rough effort range from these scope items and comparable projects.

s2d-handoff.what: Prepare the handoff from sales to delivery.
s2d-handoff.when: A signed engagement needs a receiving delivery owner.
s2d-handoff.inputs: The executed agreement, quote, deal record, and receiving team.
s2d-handoff.outputs: A handoff package with ownership, assumptions, and tracked acceptance.
s2d-handoff.example: Prepare the sales-to-delivery handoff from the executed agreement and deal record.

sales-journey-critique.what: Review a sales journey, demo, or proposed workflow.
sales-journey-critique.when: A journey needs specific corrections to steps, systems, or measures.
sales-journey-critique.inputs: The journey or demo, customer task, current workflow, and proposed change.
sales-journey-critique.outputs: A critique tracing the task and recommending supported corrections.
sales-journey-critique.example: Trace this demo against the customer’s task and recommend specific workflow corrections.

sales-process-mapping.what: Map a sales process from its source files.
sales-process-mapping.when: Ownership, triggers, handoffs, or systems of record need clarification.
sales-process-mapping.inputs: Discovery files, workbooks, CRM or Jira exports, and operating notes.
sales-process-mapping.outputs: A process explanation, diagram, ownership tables, and unresolved questions.
sales-process-mapping.example: Map the sales process from these files. Identify owners, triggers, handoffs, systems of record, and unresolved questions.

scope-reference.what: Compare scope options in a static document.
scope-reference.when: A printable scope summary or option matrix is needed.
scope-reference.inputs: One versioned quote or export with scope, hours, staffing, price, and timeline.
scope-reference.outputs: A reconciled scope summary or side-by-side option comparison.
scope-reference.example: Create a printable comparison of these options from one confirmed quote revision.

scoping-agent.what: Develop scope, effort, staffing, and timeline estimates.
scoping-agent.when: A project needs a rough range or a confirmed quote revision.
scoping-agent.inputs: The brief, scope model, comparables, rate card, and relevant constraints.
scoping-agent.outputs: Scope items and estimates with shown calculations. Unknown effort remains visible as unestimated. Staffing and schedule bounds follow the supplied capacity and dependencies.
scoping-agent.example: Estimate effort, staffing, and timing for this scope using the supplied rate card.

session-handoff.what: Prepare another session to resume the same work.
session-handoff.when: The current session is ending or needs a handoff.
session-handoff.inputs: The session’s decisions, files, running state, and completed checks.
session-handoff.outputs: A handoff with the current state, verification, open questions, and exact next action.
session-handoff.example: Prepare a handoff with the current files, decisions, verification, and exact next action.

sf-delivery-standards.what: Set up or repair a Salesforce project’s delivery checks.
sf-delivery-standards.when: The project needs delivery tooling, hooks, or operating instructions.
sf-delivery-standards.inputs: The repository, current configuration, delivery mode, and supported tools.
sf-delivery-standards.outputs: Reviewed configuration changes and evidence from the relevant checks.
sf-delivery-standards.example: Audit this Salesforce repository’s delivery hooks and project instructions.

sf-deploy-engine.what: Operate an existing Salesforce deployment pipeline.
sf-deploy-engine.when: A configured pipeline needs validation, deployment, or rollback.
sf-deploy-engine.inputs: The pipeline’s configuration, authenticated target, release state, and authorization.
sf-deploy-engine.outputs: Pipeline results and the verified state of the requested operation.
sf-deploy-engine.example: Inspect the configured pipeline and validate the selected release against its target.

sf-enterprise-patterns.what: Apply the project’s Salesforce code architecture.
sf-enterprise-patterns.when: Apex or LWC work needs service, selector, or unit-of-work conventions.
sf-enterprise-patterns.inputs: The codebase, project patterns, and the requested feature or review.
sf-enterprise-patterns.outputs: A design, implementation, or review aligned to those conventions.
sf-enterprise-patterns.example: Review this Apex change against the project’s service, selector, and unit-of-work patterns.

sf-headless-screenshot.what: Capture Salesforce UI evidence and run clickpath checks.
sf-headless-screenshot.when: An authorized UI path needs screenshots or assertions.
sf-headless-screenshot.inputs: The org connection, supported screenshot runtime, and target path.
sf-headless-screenshot.outputs: Screenshots, clickpath results, and observed UI issues.
sf-headless-screenshot.example: Capture this Salesforce clickpath and check its stated acceptance conditions.

sf-solo-devops.what: Deliver a change to a single-org Salesforce project.
sf-solo-devops.when: An authorized Salesforce change needs the project delivery workflow.
sf-solo-devops.inputs: The issue, repository, target org, configuration, and requested change.
sf-solo-devops.outputs: The change with separate validation, review, deployment, and acceptance evidence.
sf-solo-devops.example: Prepare this authorized Salesforce change using the project’s isolated delivery workflow.

skill-creation-walkthrough.what: Create a focused skill for a repeatable task.
skill-creation-walkthrough.when: A workflow needs packaging, clearer triggers, or a skill review.
skill-creation-walkthrough.inputs: The recurring task, example requests, source methods, and expected outputs.
skill-creation-walkthrough.outputs: A skill with scoped instructions, supporting resources, and validation examples.
skill-creation-walkthrough.example: Create a focused skill from this repeated workflow and these example requests.

skill-estate-sync.what: Build and audit portable skill packages.
skill-estate-sync.when: Skill source changed, an installation drifted, or a release is being prepared.
skill-estate-sync.inputs: The canonical estate checkout, dependency configuration, and target surface.
skill-estate-sync.outputs: Validated candidate packages and, when authorized, verified installation or publication records.
skill-estate-sync.example: Validate the current estate and build candidate packages without promoting them.

solution-brief.what: Explain whether a proposed solution can be delivered.
solution-brief.when: A solution needs approval, an implementation reference, or a scoping guide.
solution-brief.inputs: The solution evidence, systems, scope, interfaces, constraints, and decisions.
solution-brief.outputs: A solution brief covering delivery logic, ownership, risks, and implementation choices.
solution-brief.example: Explain whether this solution can be delivered, including systems, owners, risks, and decisions.

sow.what: Draft a statement of work from confirmed scope.
sow.when: A fixed-scope, adaptive, or assessment agreement needs drafting.
sow.inputs: The confirmed quote model and the project’s approved contract and brand profiles.
sow.outputs: A reconciled Word document and checks against the selected scope and terms.
sow.example: Draft the selected SOW variant from this confirmed quote and approved contract profile.

sow-quality.what: Review a statement of work and its obligations.
sow-quality.when: A SOW or contractual scope needs a quality review.
sow-quality.inputs: The draft agreement, confirmed scope, estimate, and controlling terms.
sow-quality.outputs: Findings or revisions addressing ambiguity, duplication, and scope consistency.
sow-quality.example: Review this SOW for ambiguous obligations and inconsistencies with the agreed scope.

spec-writer.what: Specify detailed UI, API, and data behavior.
spec-writer.when: A feature specification needs implementation detail.
spec-writer.inputs: The current implementation, user flows, interfaces, data, and constraints.
spec-writer.outputs: A detailed specification with states, persistence, interfaces, and acceptance checks.
spec-writer.example: Specify the UI states, API contracts, and data changes for this feature.

sticker-art-direction.what: Develop and critique typography-led sticker designs.
sticker-art-direction.when: A sticker concept needs composition, type exploration, or print-scale review.
sticker-art-direction.inputs: The concept, collection references, source assets, and production constraints.
sticker-art-direction.outputs: Design directions, refined compositions, and print-scale proofs.
sticker-art-direction.example: Develop distinct type treatments for this sticker concept and review them at print scale.

sticker-sheets.what: Lay out Megan’s sticker designs for Cricut printing.
sticker-sheets.when: Her PNG designs need exact-count Print Then Cut sheets.
sticker-sheets.inputs: The designs, requested sizes and counts, and her project generator.
sticker-sheets.outputs: Generated sheets and layout checks before a physical print test.
sticker-sheets.example: Lay out these PNGs in the requested sizes and counts using my current sheet generator.
sticker-sheets.reuseNote: This adapter depends on the generator maintained in Megan’s sticker project; that generator is outside this package.

system-design.what: Explore a system or service design.
system-design.when: A working architecture or technical trade-off discussion is needed.
system-design.inputs: The problem, requirements, constraints, scale, and existing system context.
system-design.outputs: A working design covering components, data, interfaces, and trade-offs.
system-design.example: Explore a working design for this service, including its data flow and trade-offs.

team-onboarding.what: Plan a role’s first 30, 60, and 90 days.
team-onboarding.when: A new starter or team transition needs a structured ramp.
team-onboarding.inputs: The role, success criteria, mentors, existing materials, access, and time budget.
team-onboarding.outputs: A role-specific onboarding plan with learning, contribution, and feedback milestones.
team-onboarding.example: Create a 30/60/90-day plan for this role using the team’s mentoring and access constraints.

transcript-ingestion.what: Preserve and index a meeting transcript.
transcript-ingestion.when: A transcript or recording export needs a durable project record.
transcript-ingestion.inputs: The original transcript and confirmed client, opportunity, or engagement identity.
transcript-ingestion.outputs: A preserved source, normalized transcript, and indexed meeting record.
transcript-ingestion.example: Preserve and index this transcript under its confirmed opportunity and meeting identity.

uat-validation.what: Track acceptance testing and release readiness.
uat-validation.when: A delivery engagement needs test coverage or a go or no-go packet.
uat-validation.inputs: Executed scope, requirements, test results, defects, and gate owners.
uat-validation.outputs: Test scripts, traceability, defect and coverage records, and readiness findings.
uat-validation.example: Build the acceptance test and coverage records from these approved requirements.

usability-testing.what: Plan usability research or synthesize observations.
usability-testing.when: A team needs participant tasks, sessions, or findings.
usability-testing.inputs: The research questions, interface, participant context, and supplied observations.
usability-testing.outputs: A session plan, neutral task scripts, or supported usability findings.
usability-testing.example: Write neutral participant tasks for these research questions and this interface.

writing-integrity.what: Review prose for clarity, meaning, and the intended voice.
writing-integrity.when: Writing needs drafting, revision, review, or a retained correction.
writing-integrity.inputs: The brief or draft, controlling sources, and an authorized profile when available.
writing-integrity.outputs: Complete reviewed prose and, when enabled, private correction-learning records.
writing-integrity.example: Review this draft for clarity, repetition, and unsupported claims. Preserve its meaning and intended voice; return the complete revision.

writing-style-builder.what: Build or revise a person’s private writing profile.
writing-style-builder.when: Someone authorizes a profile from their writing samples.
writing-style-builder.inputs: Authorized samples, the intended author, profile scope, and confirmation.
writing-style-builder.outputs: A reviewed private profile with supported style rules and update controls.
writing-style-builder.example: Build a draft style profile from these authorized samples and identify the rules I need to confirm.
